::: {.manual-status}
**Resource status:** Usable broad-beta. Adapt the fields to the evidence type and selected review method. Do not store copyrighted, confidential, identifiable or culturally restricted material in an inappropriate location.
:::

## Use this at two different moments

**Triage** decides whether an item deserves fuller attention. **Extraction** records what an included source contributes to a named question. Do not treat a title-and-abstract screen as source verification.

## Blank triage record

**Record ID:** [ ]
**Verified citation or stable link:** [ ]
**Question this source may answer:** [ ]
**Evidence or source type:** [ ]
**Population, setting, period or corpus:** [ ]
**Apparent relevance:** high / possible / low
**Credibility or fit warnings:** [ ]
**Decision:** retrieve / include / hold / exclude
**Reason and reviewer/date:** [ ]

## Blank extraction record

**Source's own purpose or question:** [ ]
**Design, approach or form of argument:** [ ]
**Materials, participants, sources or cases:** [ ]
**Relevant finding, evidence or reasoning:** [ ]
**Exact location:** [page, section, table, figure, timestamp or dataset location]
**Authors' interpretation:** [ ]
**My interpretation:** [label inference explicitly]
**Limitations stated by authors:** [ ]
**Additional limitations or applicability boundaries:** [ ]
**Contradictory or qualifying evidence to seek:** [ ]
**How this changes the present argument or decision:** [ ]
**Use:** cite / compare / background only / exclude

## Completed example

**Record ID:** FEED-014
**Verified citation:** Hattie, J. and Timperley, H. (2007), “The Power of Feedback”, *Review of Educational Research*, 77(1), 81–112, DOI verified.
**Question this source may answer:** What makes feedback actionable?
**Evidence type:** broad educational review and conceptual model.
**Population and setting:** educational research across levels; not specifically doctoral supervision.
**Decision:** include for mechanism, not for a doctorate-specific effect estimate.

**Relevant reasoning:** feedback is framed in relation to goals, current performance and next actions.
**Exact location:** model and discussion sections checked in the full article.
**Authors' interpretation:** feedback varies in effectiveness depending on the information conveyed and its level.
**My interpretation:** the model can structure a doctoral feedback conversation, but transfer to doctoral settings is an inference.
**Applicability boundary:** do not claim that all feedback improves doctoral outcomes.
**Use:** compare with doctorate-specific evidence and cite only for the bounded conceptual claim.

## Scenario test

You find a review stating that an intervention “improves performance”, but the included studies use different outcomes and short follow-up periods. Record the review's exact conclusion, the outcome variation and follow-up boundary. Do not extract the simplified universal sentence. If that stronger claim matters, inspect the underlying evidence.
